oil.summary: Crude markets surged on compounding Middle East supply shocks. WTI jumped 3.88% to $105.32 and Brent added 2.54% to $108.36 after Saudi Aramco suspended Yanbu Red Sea loadings following the shutdown of the East-West pipeline, cutting off a critical export artery to European refiners. The Hormuz corridor remains under stress: an Iranian vessel was struck in the strait, Houthis are expanding control of the shipping lane, and Iran is maintaining its oil blockade pending cessation of attacks — a posture that has opened a $40-plus spread between regional crude grades. The Russia-Ukraine conflict adds a further layer, with overnight strikes hitting a Ukrainian oil refinery. A large 7.14-million-barrel API crude inventory build offered a partial counterweight, as did U.S. Energy Secretary Wright's comment that the Saudi pipeline could return within days. RBOB gasoline bucked the trend, falling 2.26%.
drivers: Saudi Aramco suspends Yanbu loadings and cancels European cargoes after East-West pipeline shutdown, tightening Atlantic Basin supply
Iran maintains Hormuz blockade; Houthi expansion in shipping lane and tanker strike sustain $40-plus crude grade risk premium
API reports a 7.14-million-barrel U.S. crude inventory build, capping upside; U.S. Energy Secretary signals potential near-term Saudi pipeline restart

gas.summary: Natural gas price action was divergent on either side of the Atlantic. Henry Hub edged up 1.66% to $2.944/MMBtu, a modest move supported by the broader energy complex tightness rather than any gas-specific domestic catalyst — news flow was thin on U.S. gas fundamentals beyond a reminder that Texas accounted for over a quarter of U.S. gross withdrawals of 47.7 trillion cubic feet in 2025. TTF fell 3.77% to €79.455/MWh in a likely technical pullback after a sharp 29.35% monthly rally; Saudi Aramco's cancellation of European crude cargoes and continued Russia-Ukraine strikes — including a hit on a gas station — sustain underlying European supply anxiety even as spot prices corrected today. Headlines data for gas-specific drivers were limited.
drivers: TTF retreats 3.77% on the day after a 29.35% monthly surge, suggesting near-term profit-taking despite unresolved European supply risks
Ongoing Russia-Ukraine strikes, including infrastructure hits, maintain geopolitical risk premium for European gas markets
Henry Hub gains are modest and gas-specific U.S. catalysts thin; Texas dominance of domestic production (>25% of 2025 output) underpins supply adequacy narrative

power.summary: EU carbon allowances extended their grind higher, adding 2.87% to $83.795/EUA, supported by the broader energy price rally and persistent geopolitical tension that complicates the European power fuel mix. The monthly gain of 6.87% in EUAs tracks the sharp rise in TTF, though today's TTF pullback provided some relief to carbon-linked generation costs. On structural themes, Chinese solar panel prices have collapsed to $0.12/watt, accelerating rooftop installations globally and carrying long-run implications for peak power demand and carbon intensity. U.S. grid resilience is under fresh scrutiny: FERC issued a summer deadline to utilities around AI-driven load growth, and separately, AI-enabled cyberattacks are flagged as a growing threat to critical energy infrastructure. BRICS nations are also pushing back on Western influence over energy and economic frameworks.
drivers: EU carbon EUAs up 2.87% on the day, tracking elevated energy complex prices; monthly gain of 6.87% aligns with TTF's 29.35% monthly surge
Chinese solar panel prices at $0.12/watt driving global rooftop installation surge, with long-term implications for power demand profiles and carbon intensity
U.S. grid resilience in focus as FERC sets AI load-growth deadlines for utilities and AI-enabled cyberattacks are identified as a rising threat to power infrastructure
